bug_semantics: createVerifier reuses caller-supplied RegExp objects for allowedAud/allowedIss/allowedSub/allowedJti/allowedNonce. ensureStringClaimMatcher() returns those objects unchanged, and validateClaimValues() calls a.test(v) without resetting lastIndex. With /g or /y the same valid token therefore alternates pass/fail (logical DoS / auth flapping). Invalid tokens are not accepted.
flaw_origin: First write of src/verifier.js in the library's initial commit: ensureStringClaimMatcher mapped any value with a test() method through as-is (including RegExp), and claim validation used allowed.some(a => a.test(value)) with no lastIndex reset. Later commits (including b1d71ed6 string-matcher exactness and c4d4580 spec alignment) kept that passthrough; they did not introduce the stateful-test bug.
evidence: CVE-2026-35040 is PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected). Advisory GHSA-3j8v-cgw4-2g6q and NVD describe non-deterministic allowed-claim validation from stateful /g or /y RegExp. Direct fix 18d25904e4617e8753526d1b3ab5a2cccdea726a (PR #593, parent e07b1fd23f02a47f1be677a21a4f07607b478e66) wraps RegExp matchers so lastIndex is reset before test(); pre-fix parent still returned raw test() objects. git log -S 'ensureStringClaimMatcher' and -S 'a.test(v)' on src/verifier.js both bottom out at 51fe1ea3feacb931cd66b0f915b046cbeab88790 (feat(wip): Initial version). git cat-file -e 5063678a36ff118da9671f1f1df3d67cc95d1169:src/verifier.js fails (path absent on parent). BIC object: author/committer Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>, message 'feat(wip): Initial version.', no Co-Authored-By/Generated-with/bot author. git log -1 --format='%an %ae %cn %ce' on BIC: Shogun shogun@cowtech.it Shogun shogun@cowtech.it.
reasoning: Real vulnerability: library-accepted RegExp matchers plus unreset lastIndex make verification non-deterministic for /g and /y. BIC is the smallest surviving first-write of those matcher lines (initial src/verifier.js). Parent tree lacks the path. BIC authorship is human (Shogun) with no AI markers on the commit object.
